subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: Worked: inverse via conjugate & a modulus proof

board_content.text: Inverse from z-bar over |z|^2, and prove via modulus
Now prove: if $a+ib=\dfrac{c+i}{c-i}$ with $c$ real, then $a^{2}+b^{2}=1$.
Take the modulus of both sides — moduli are multiplicative.
Taking $|\cdot|$ across a quotient beats expanding into $a+ib$.

segments_english.text: Two examples that show off the conjugate-and-modulus toolkit in action.
First, the inverse of z equals four minus three i, but now using the clean formula. The modulus squared is sixteen plus nine, twenty five. The conjugate is four plus three i.
So z inverse is z bar over modulus squared: four plus three i over twenty five, which is four twenty-fifths plus three twenty-fifths i.
Now a proof. Suppose a plus i b equals c plus i, over c minus i, where c is real. Show that a squared plus b squared equals one.
The elegant move is to take the modulus of both sides, because modulus is multiplicative and splits across the quotient.
On the right, the top has modulus root c squared plus one, and the bottom has the very same modulus, root c squared plus one. They cancel to give one.
So the modulus of a plus i b is one, meaning root of a squared plus b squared equals one, hence a squared plus b squared equals one. Proof complete.
Notice how much work we skipped: taking the modulus across the quotient was far faster than expanding the fraction into a plus i b form.

segments_hinglish.text: Do examples jo conjugate-and-modulus toolkit ko action mein dikhate hain.
Pehle, z equals four minus three i ka inverse, par ab clean formula use karke. Modulus squared hai sixteen plus nine, twenty five. Conjugate hai four plus three i.
To z inverse hai z bar over modulus squared: four plus three i over twenty five, jo hai four twenty-fifths plus three twenty-fifths i.
Ab ek proof. Maano a plus i b barabar c plus i, over c minus i, jahan c real hai. Dikhao ki a square plus b square barabar one.
Elegant move hai dono taraf ka modulus lena, kyunki modulus multiplicative hai aur quotient par split ho jaata hai.
Right par, top ka modulus hai root c square plus one, aur bottom ka bilkul wahi modulus, root c square plus one. Wo cancel hoke dete hain one.
To a plus i b ka modulus hai one, matlab a square plus b square ka root barabar one, isliye a square plus b square barabar one. Proof poora.
Dekho kitna kaam bach gaya: quotient par modulus lena fraction ko a plus i b form mein expand karne se kaafi tez tha.
